items.title: A missed medical appointment
items.situation: You had an appointment with a specialist at the local hospital yesterday morning. You had waited four months for it, but you wrote the wrong date in your diary and did not realise until the hospital sent a text saying you had missed it. The next available appointment is in another three months. You have phoned the clinic and are speaking to the receptionist. What would you say to the receptionist?
points: Apologise and take responsibility for the mistake
Explain briefly why you need to be seen soon
Ask whether an earlier or cancellation appointment is possible
Thank the receptionist for any help

items.title: A cancelled connecting flight
items.situation: You are at an airport on your way home from a holiday. Your connecting flight has just been cancelled because of a technical fault, and the airline says the next available flight is in two days. You have an important job interview the day after tomorrow, and you have no hotel booked. You are now at the airline's service desk, speaking to a member of staff. What would you say to the member of staff?
points: Stay polite and explain your situation clearly
Mention why the timing matters
Ask about alternative routes or other airlines
Ask what accommodation and meals the airline will provide

items.title: The wrong hotel room
items.situation: You booked and paid in advance for a double room with a sea view at a seaside hotel for your anniversary. When you open the door to your room, you find it is a small single room overlooking the car park, and the air conditioning is not working. The hotel booking confirmation is on your phone. You have gone back down to the reception desk. What would you say to the receptionist?
points: Explain calmly what you booked and what you received
Refer to the confirmation as evidence
Mention the air conditioning as a separate problem
Ask for the correct room or a clear alternative, such as a partial refund

items.title: Unclear medicine instructions
items.situation: Your doctor prescribed you some tablets yesterday and told you to take two a day. However, the label on the box from the pharmacy says to take one tablet three times a day with food. You are also taking a medicine for hay fever, and you are not sure whether the two can be taken together. You have gone back to the pharmacy to speak to the pharmacist. What would you say to the pharmacist?
points: Explain the difference between what the doctor said and the label
Ask which instruction to follow
Mention the other medicine and ask about combining them
Check that you have understood the answer

items.title: A friend avoiding the doctor
items.situation: Your friend Ryan has had a painful knee for over a month. He has been taking painkillers and still goes running three times a week, but the pain is getting worse and he now limps after every run. He refuses to see a doctor because he says it is a waste of time and they will only tell him to rest. You are walking home together after watching a film. What would you say to Ryan?
points: Show concern rather than lecturing
Point out that the pain is getting worse
Explain the risk of long-term damage
Suggest a practical first step, such as booking an appointment together

items.title: An unwanted tour upgrade
items.situation: You are on a guided coach tour abroad. The tour guide, Mr Costa, has announced an optional excursion to a wine estate tomorrow, costing sixty euros, and has told you personally that it is the highlight of the trip and that you will regret missing it. You do not drink alcohol, you are on a tight budget, and you had planned a quiet day exploring the town on foot. What would you say to Mr Costa?
points: Thank him for the suggestion politely
Decline clearly without over-explaining
Give a brief reason
Ask for a recommendation for your own day in the town

items.title: A lost passport abroad
items.situation: You are travelling abroad with your friend Mia. This afternoon she discovered that her passport has gone missing, probably stolen from her bag at a busy market. Your flight home is in four days. Mia is in tears, saying she will be stuck in the country for weeks and will lose her job. You know that embassies can issue emergency travel documents quickly. What would you say to Mia?
points: Calm her down and show you are there to help
Explain that emergency travel documents exist
Set out clear next steps, such as a police report and contacting the embassy
Offer to go with her

items.title: Returning a faulty coffee machine
items.situation: Five weeks ago you bought an expensive coffee machine from an electrical shop. It has now stopped heating water. You have the receipt, but the shop's policy allows refunds only within thirty days. The assistant has offered to send the machine away for repair, which could take a month. You would prefer a replacement or a refund because you use the machine every day. What would you say to the assistant?
points: Explain the fault and when you bought it
Acknowledge the store policy
Argue that a product should not fail so quickly
Propose an acceptable outcome, such as a replacement or a loan machine

items.title: Ending a gym contract early
items.situation: Six months ago you signed a twelve-month contract with a gym. Your employer has now moved you to an office in another city, two hundred miles away, starting next month. The contract says members can leave early only for medical reasons, and the gym has told you that you must keep paying until the end of the year. You are meeting the gym manager, Mrs Hale. What would you say to Mrs Hale?
points: Explain the relocation clearly and offer evidence
Show that the move is outside your control
Ask whether an exception can be made
Suggest alternatives, such as transferring the membership or a reduced fee

items.title: Sleepless before the exams
items.situation: Your housemate Zara has important exams next week. For several nights she has been studying until three in the morning, drinking energy drinks to stay awake, and then struggling to sleep. Today she says she cannot concentrate, she keeps forgetting what she has read, and she feels constantly exhausted. She asks you if you have any ideas that might help. What advice would you give Zara?
points: Show sympathy for how she feels
Explain the link between sleep and memory
Suggest practical changes, such as cutting caffeine and fixed study hours
Recommend short breaks, and seeing a doctor if it continues
